PRICES. Every `last_price` here is the 2026-10-06 close, fetched in the pre-market session with an age of ~879 minutes. At this hour that is the freshest honest equity price, not stale data — a closed market is a closed market. No price in this report is an estimate.

INDEPENDENT RECOMPUTATION. Every reward-to-risk ratio and every stop distance was recomputed at synthesis from the final levels and from freshly fetched atr14, not carried over from the research notes. All nine clear their floor (2.0 swing, 2.5 long-term, measured for DG against its stated 99.57 bear case rather than a stop), and all eight swing stops clear the 2.0-ATR floor. The recomputation agreed with the research log on all nine — which is worth saying, because the pipeline exists on the assumption that it will not.

WHERE THE RATIOS SIT. Two of nine land just above their floor (AZZ 2.07, LULU 2.07), which is the signature CLAUDE.md warns about — targets nudged until they pass. Checked from the other side, it is not that here: AZZ's stop is 2.82 ATR and LULU's is 3.37 ATR, so neither ratio was bought with a tightened stop. DAL is the one to watch: its stop is 2.02 ATR, sitting directly on the floor, and it cannot be widened without breaking the ratio — so it clears both tests with no margin on either.

THE STOP-DISTANCE CAVEAT THAT MATTERS MOST. Five of the nine are updates to positions already FILLED, so their entries are historical facts and cannot be moved. Their stop distances are measured in ATRs from that original entry, which is the right denominator for the trade — but for the two deeply underwater longs it flatters the live risk. Measured from TODAY's price instead: LCII's stop is 1.46 ATR away and KHC's is 1.53 ATR, both BELOW the 2.0 floor, and both names sit ~1.3% above their 120-day lows. These stops are placed below those lows on structure, and the alternative was leaving the positions with no stop at all, which strategy.md forbids — so they are published. But size them knowing that ordinary daily range can reach them, which is exactly how all ten of this report's first closed stop-outs died.

COMPOSITION, AND WHY IT IS SKEWED. Only TWO ideas are new — AZZ (rank 1) and DG (rank 3). The other seven are position updates, and five of those exist purely to supply a downside the position did not have: six open longs were carrying no stop at all and three of them were within 3% of their 120-day lows. That is the honest output of this tape rather than a shortfall of effort, and position updates are management of existing risk, not new risk.

HORIZON AND ASSET-CLASS SKEW. 8 swing, 1 long-term, ZERO intraday; and 9 of 9 are single stocks (7 long, 2 short). No quota was applied in either direction and nothing was padded or trimmed. Each absence has a stated reason: no intraday idea cleared because the day's one large move was a nuclear-power repricing that had already gapped 7-12% before the open, and with no VIX, no index quote and no options-implied move there was no basis for a same-session level. Crypto and crypto futures were refused because coingecko returns only 4-day bars beyond 30 days, so the 2.5-ATR stop floor cannot be computed. Event contracts were refused because the Fed and CPI ladders price the Fed's own dot plot efficiently and the U-3 ladder's spreads are 7-10 cents. The rate-sensitive ETF shorts (TLT, IYR, ITB) were refused because their published entries now sit above a market 1-3% off three-month lows, and chasing a short into a low is the mirror of the reflex-discount entry.

READ THAT SKEW AGAINST THE TRACK RECORD. prior_context shows single stocks 0/7 versus ETFs 2/5, and conviction-2 ideas 0/3 at -6.4%. Today is nine for nine single stocks and three of them are conviction 2. The sample is 12 closed trades, under the ~15 threshold where it stops being noise, so it is not treated as a verdict — but a report that is entirely in the bucket with the worst record should say so plainly rather than smooth it over, and the three conviction-2 ideas are sized at 1% each for exactly that reason.

CORRELATION — AT THE CAP, NOT OVER IT. The three conviction-2 longs are substantially ONE BET: KHC is part of the bond-proxy complex (the same de-rating as XLU, IYR, TLT and PEP), while LCII and BCC are rate-sensitive consumer durables and building products. All three need the discount rate to stop rising, all three are within 1-16% of their 120-day lows, and the Fed is priced 71% to hike by December. Three ideas on one driver is exactly strategy.md's limit and not a breach, but at 1% each they are 3% of capital on a single macro outcome that current pricing says goes the other way. Note also that ranks 5 and 6 (LULU and NKE shorts) are one bet on US discretionary apparel demand — two, under the cap.

SIZING. All nine respect the caps. The three conviction-2 ideas are 1% each; ranks 1-6 run 2-3%. AZZ is the only conviction 5 and is sized 2% rather than the 4-5% its tier would allow, because its average dollar volume is just $33.4M — the exit test, not the entry, is what binds on a name that thin. Its `risk_tier` is recorded as `standard` to match the size actually recommended rather than the conviction score.

CONVICTION IS COUNTED, NOT FELT. Every score equals its number of distinct evidence kinds — spread 2:3, 3:1, 4:4, 5:1. No candidate needed its score lowered at synthesis. That is deliberately not the collapse-to-3 pattern CLAUDE.md records from the first 57 ideas, where 39 scored 3.

ONE IDEA SAYS DO NOT BUY IT TODAY. DG carries `wait: true`. At the 123.27 market its reward-to-risk is 0.63 and fails the 2.5 long-term floor outright; at the 110.00 limit it is 2.66 and clears. The target was NOT raised to make today's price work — the entry moved and the valuation did not. It also amends a pending DG buy at 134.50 from 2026-08-21 that was set above the 120-day high of 134.125 and could therefore never have filled, which is a defect worth naming in its own right. DG carries no stop, which the long-term lane permits, so its invalidation is explicit instead: comps negative two quarters running, OR traffic negative in any quarter while comps stay positive on ticket alone.

TWO OFFSETTING PAIRS THE SCHEMA CANNOT EXPRESS. The book is simultaneously long AND short both LULU and NKE — LULU long @115.00 and short @100.61, NKE long @40.75 and short @38.40 — so net exposure in each is about zero while paying two sets of financing. In both cases the short is profitable and the long is deeply underwater, which is the market's verdict on which side was right, and the researched evidence (published here as ranks 5 and 6) is on the short. The recommendation is to CLOSE THE LONG LEG of each pair in state/open_positions.json. catalyst.action: hold the existing position; do not add above 94.50, and treat any retest of the 10-06 gap base at 89.50-91.00 as the add level

recommendations.thesis: UPDATE TO AN EXISTING POSITION opened 2026-08-17 at 94.00, now 93.02, and the hold is justified by information that did not exist when it was opened. Brookfield and Cameco announced on 2026-09-30 a US-Korea framework committing up to 120B USD of Korean investment toward eight large US reactors, under which Westinghouse receives an upfront payment, guaranteed scope of work and a long-term fuel-fabrication contract, with Korea taking a 5-10% cornerstone equity stake. Cameco owns 49% of Westinghouse, which is the transmission mechanism, and the whole fuel cycle repriced on it: CCJ gapped from 89.55 to a 93.02 close on 10-06 while LEU +8.8%, UEC +8.1%, BWXT +7.6% and URA +4.0% did the same thing the same session.
recommendations.key_risk: The framework is explicitly non-binding and subject to final negotiation, so the entire 10-06 re-rating can be given back on a single headline about Korean terms slipping, with no company-specific news required. The 135.00 target is also above the 120-day high of 131.21, so it needs the stock to round-trip a six-month range rather than just extend. RED TEAM ON THE TARGET: 135.00 is 12.33 ATR from the 94.00 entry, against a 6.0 ATR guide for a 15-session swing, and sits above the 120-day high of 131.21. That is not a swing target, it is a six-month target on a swing clock, and the 3.57:1 ratio is built on it. Judge this position over the next three weeks on whether the 10-06 gap base at 89.50-91.00 holds - not on progress toward 135.00, which nothing in the next fifteen sessions is likely to deliver. From the 93.02 close the live ratio is 3.99:1, so the arithmetic is not the problem; the time horizon attached to it is.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that a non-binding memorandum is worth nothing and the first concrete reactor is years out, so this is sentiment rather than cash flow. The partial answer is that World Nuclear News reports the framework carries a 10B USD Korean advance payment due by the end of 2026 for long-lead items and roughly 2B USD of Westinghouse value per APR1400 unit through IP licensing, engineering, procurement and fuel fabrication - that is a dated cash transfer rather than an intention. It is only a partial answer, which is why this is held and not added to. RED TEAM ON WHETHER THE EDGE IS STILL THERE: the framework is dated 2026-09-30 and the entire fuel cycle repriced on it in a single session on 10-06 - CCJ +3.9% off a 89.55 gap, LEU +8.8%, UEC +8.1%, BWXT +7.6%, URA +4.0%. The information that justifies the hold is a week old and one full day of re-rating is already behind it, so this is being right rather than being early, and the asymmetry is smaller than it was on 09-30. Also note the sourcing is weaker than the evidence claims: the `primary_document` entry says "Read the Brookfield Asset Management release" but points at a manilatimes.net AMP republication of the GlobeNewswire wire copy, not at Brookfield's or Cameco's own filing. Conviction held at 4 because the three evidence kinds are genuinely independent sources and the thesis is falsifiable on a dated fact - the 10B USD Korean advance payment for long-lead items either lands by end-2026 or it does not.

recommendations.thesis: Dollar General reported Q2 FY2026 on 2026-08-27 with net sales up 5.2% to 11.3B, same-store sales up 3.5%, operating profit up 29.2% to 769.2M and diluted EPS up 33.3% to 2.48, and raised FY2026 EPS guidance to 7.80-8.00 from 7.20-7.45. That is the trade-down mechanism working in real time, and the macro I found today - a 10-year at 5.275%, the highest since 2002, with consumer durables being destroyed around it at WHR -49.1% and LCII -40.5% - is the condition under which it keeps working. Anchoring the downside at a price actually printed this quarter, rather than at a modelled one, is what makes the 2.66 reward-to-risk at a 110.00 entry real - and the same arithmetic at 123.27 gives 0.63, which is why today is not the day. RED TEAM: conviction lowered 4 -> 3. `primary_document` and `valuation_anchor` cite the identical Morningstar/Business Wire URL, so three kinds rest on two distinct sources, and the second is a finnhub positioning read that is itself bearish - 45.0% bullish and deteriorating with 21 holds. SEPARATELY, A MECHANICAL POINT THE READER CANNOT SEE: because this idea carries catalyst.wait = true, publish_sheets skips it entirely, so the stated amendment of the 2026-08-21 pending entry does NOT reach the tracker - that row still carries 134.50 and will expire unfilled on its own schedule. That is the right outcome rather than a bug: a 134.50 momentum-breakout buy and a 110.00 value-accumulation buy are different trades, and the second should open its own row when it fills rather than inherit the first one's date.
